learning_outcomes.text: The student will understand the importance of the company as an actor in an economic system, specifying the concept of a company, its objectives, and the main functions it performs.
They will gain a global vision of the company, highlighting the functional areas that comprise it and the need for integration and coordination between the different existing decision-making areas.
They will acquire knowledge and tools to help them manage a business organization, delving into a company's operations, financial, and commercial decisions.

syllabus_topics: Operational needs for funds and working capital
Introduction, objectives and policies of human resource management
Productivity as a basic objective of Operations Management

assessment_methods.method: Written test (final exam and/or partial cumulative/eliminatory exams)
Exploitation of practical activities carried out in: classroom, laboratory, computer room, field, visits, etc.
Resolution and delivery of activities (cases, problems, reports, assignments, projects, etc.), individually and/or in groups

assessment_rules: For ordinary evaluation (continuous assessment), the final written test accounts for 70% of the final grade, and the resolution and submission of activities accounts for 30%. The written test must be passed with a minimum score of 5 out of 10 to pass the course. If the written test score is less than 5, the final course grade will be the written test score. For global evaluation (without continuous assessment), a global final exam evaluates 100% of the competencies, with a written test component accounting for 80% and the resolution and submission of problems, assignments, or practical cases for 20%. A minimum score of 5 out of 10 is required for the written test component in the global evaluation, and the final course grade must be 5 or higher to pass.
